summary: PARTIAL is the right status, but the auditor's details need two corrections. (1) 'No blocking defect' is wrong. The new remembered-preferences fast path (65af92766) applies the node's background answer only if the composer draft object is identical to the one it seeded. ChatComposer replaces that object on mount (its image-persist effect calls clearPersistedAttachments, which has no no-op guard). So whenever the preferences RPC returns after the draft view mounts (typical on remote saved environments), the correction is silently dropped and the draft keeps stale defaults. Nothing invalidates the remembered cache when the user saves project defaults, so the next New thread after a settings change opens with the old model/env mode. The browser test mocks navigate, so it never mounts ChatView and misses this. (2) The remaining waterfall is narrower than 'hosted nodes and hosted-hub web'. nodeIdForHostedEnvironment is stubbed to null in the standard build, so only the hosted-hub web build still pays the fresh ~100 KB getConfig on every fresh draft (in parallel with preferences when the cached primary config shows the capability). Desktop Hub-relay workspace nodes use their own per-environment saved-runtime config with no getConfig. Everything else the auditor credited is verified: the route-chunk preload at click time, cached config for non-hosted targets, the boot-time duplicate getConfig removed, and the resolveAvailableEditors cache. A smaller duplicate of the same sequential getConfig-then-preferences read remains in the PR agent handoff (agentHandoff.ts readDraftDefaults), mostly hidden behind the change-request fetch.

evidence.note: nodeIdForHostedEnvironment returns null in the standard build, so `hosted` is true only in the hosted-hub web build. Desktop Hub workspace nodes take the cached path.

Desktop workspace (Hub relay) connections feed a per-environment, identity-normalised serverConfig from their own subscribeConfig stream into the saved runtime store. readEnvironmentServerConfig reads that store, so no getConfig runs on desktop.

Non-hosted fast path: a cached config plus a remembered answer opens the draft with no RPC, and the preferences read runs in the background as `fresh`. Without a remembered answer, only the small preferences RPC is awaited (1 RTT on the first draft per project per session).
Hosted-web path still awaits the full getConfig. Preferences run in parallel only when the cached primary config shows the capability; otherwise the two reads are sequential.
The background answer applies only if getComposerDraft(draftId) === seeded.composer and the session object is unchanged (whole-object identity).
The image-persist effect runs on mount and calls clearComposerDraftPersistedAttachments(composerDraftTarget) whenever composerImages is empty.

clearPersistedAttachments always writes {...current, persistedAttachments: [], nonPersistedImageIds: []}, a new object even when nothing changes. The identity guard therefore fails after the composer mounts.
On a draft route the composer target is the draftId, the same key the seed captured. ChatComposer renders unconditionally (ChatView.tsx:6070).
The test that 'applies the node's newer answer' mocks navigate, so ChatView/ChatComposer never mount and the mount-time rewrite race is not covered.
Saving project defaults updates server settings but never refreshes or forgets the effectivePreferencesCache in newDraftDefaults.ts:27. The next New thread opens with the pre-change answer.
Account-scoped teardown does not clear the module-level effectivePreferencesCache (low risk: keys include environmentId).

Hosted deactivate disconnects the primary, clears server state and nulls the primary descriptor before the next node activates. That is the basis for a generation-stamped cached config on hosted, which needs a decision.

PR agent handoff readDraftDefaults still runs a full getConfig and then preferences sequentially for every target, duplicating logic readNewDraftDefaults already has. It runs in Promise.all with the change-request detail read (line 289), so it is mostly hidden.
Boot-time duplicate getConfig removed; startServerStateSync relies on the subscribeConfig snapshot only.
resolveAvailableEditors cached for 5 min keyed on platform+PATH; loadServerConfig (apps/server/src/ws/context.ts:1195) uses it.

remaining: (a) Hosted-hub web build only: every fresh draft still awaits a fresh full getConfig (~85-130 KB plus 1 relay RTT, about 100-400 ms, and a long decode frame at 4x CPU). See useHandleNewThread.ts:160 and newDraftDefaults.ts:125-135. The remembered-preferences fast path is disabled there (newDraftDefaults.ts:113), and when the cached primary config lacks the capability the reads stay sequential. (b) Non-hosted: the first fresh draft per project per session still waits 1 preferences RTT before navigating (newDraftDefaults.ts:122). The proposal's full 'navigate first, fill defaults later' is only applied to repeat drafts. (c) agentHandoff.ts:176-199 duplicates the sequential getConfig and preferences read for every target, mostly hidden behind the change-request fetch.
fixDefects: 1) The background correction is dropped in the real app. useHandleNewThread.ts:202-206 compares whole composer and session object identity. ChatComposer's mount effect (ChatComposer.tsx:1444-1449) calls clearPersistedAttachments, which always replaces the composer draft object (draftStore.ts:2245-2255, no no-op guard). If the background getProjectPreferences returns after the draft route mounts (typical on remote saved environments, possible locally under load), the node's current answer is ignored. The draft keeps the remembered model and env mode even though the user never touched it. The browser test mocks navigate and does not catch this (NewThreadSettings.browser.tsx:222-272). 2) The remembered cache (newDraftDefaults.ts:27) is never invalidated when project or node defaults are saved (ProjectPreferenceSettings.tsx:119-152) or when a settingsUpdated config event arrives. Combined with defect 1, the first New thread after a user changes the project default model or env mode on a remote node opens with the old values; later drafts are correct. 3) Minor: the cache is not cleared on hosted account teardown (hostedHub/environment.ts:58). Low risk because keys are environment-scoped.
implementationSketch: Defect fix (S, no decision): (1) In packages/client-runtime/src/state/composer/draftStore.ts clearPersistedAttachments, return `state` unchanged when current.persistedAttachments.length === 0 && current.nonPersistedImageIds.length === 0. This also removes a pointless store write and re-render on every composer mount. Audit syncPersistedAttachments for the same pattern. (2) In apps/web/src/hooks/useHandleNewThread.ts createAndOpenDraft, replace the whole-object identity guard with a field-level 'untouched' check. Capture the seeded values the seed writes: composer.modelSelectionByProvider, composer.activeProvider, session.envMode/branch/worktreePath/tokenMode/runtimeMode. Compare those references or values in the background `.then`, so unrelated writes such as attachments, upload tokens or prompt typing no longer block the correction. Decide whether prompt typing should still block it; it probably should not, since it is not a defaults field. (3) Add `forgetRememberedProjectPreferences(environmentId, projectId?)` in apps/web/src/hooks/newDraftDefaults.ts (or refresh through readAndRememberProjectPreferences). Call it from ProjectPreferenceSettings.save on success. Clear an environment's entries when a settingsUpdated config event arrives: hook applySettingsUpdated/applyServerConfigEvent for the primary and onConfigUpdated with type settingsUpdated in environments/runtime/service.ts for saved environments. Clear the whole map in clearWebHostedAccountScopedState. Tests: extend NewThreadSettings.browser.tsx so the second draft calls useComposerDraftStore.getState().clearPersistedAttachments(draftId) (simulating the composer mount) before resolveAnswer and still expects envMode 'local' / 'newer-model'. Add a unit test that saving project defaults makes the next readNewDraftDefaults await a fresh read. Add a draftStore unit test that clearPersistedAttachments on an already-empty draft keeps object identity. Hosted remainder (M, needs decision): in hosted-hub web, record the primary config together with the hosted mutation lease's selectionGeneration when the current primary connection's subscribeConfig snapshot is applied (ServerStateBootstrap/startServerStateSync, or a hosted-only wrapper keyed by environmentId). In readNewDraftDefaults, accept that cached config when its stamp equals readHostedNodeMutationLease(env)?.selectionGeneration, and use requireFreshConfig only when it is absent or mismatched. Then let hosted use the remembered-preferences-plus-background-refresh route; the lease check before/after at useHandleNewThread.ts:163-170 stays. Alternative: a light `server.getNewDraftDefaults` RPC returning defaultThreadEnvMode, defaultAgentTokenMode, chats availability, projectPreferences capability and effective preferences, with an 'Unknown request tag' fallback to getConfig. That is a contracts, server and rpcAccessPolicy change and may need a Hub pin bump for relay policy. Optionally switch agentHandoff.ts readDraftDefaults to readNewDraftDefaults to remove the duplicated logic.
decisionReason: The defect fixes (draftStore no-op guard, field-level untouched check, cache invalidation) need no decision. Removing the fresh getConfig on hosted-hub web does: it means trusting a cached config snapshot under the hosted lifecycle rules in AGENTS.md ('stale generations cannot publish ... snapshots'), which the code comments deliberately avoid today. The light-RPC alternative is a protocol/contracts change that may need a Hub pin bump and deploy.
correction: The auditor reported no blocking defect, but the remembered-preferences fast path has a real correctness gap. Its background correction is defeated by ChatComposer's mount-time clearPersistedAttachments rewrite (whole-object identity guard, no no-op guard in the store), and the remembered cache is never invalidated when defaults are saved. The auditor also over-scoped the remainder to 'hosted nodes': in the standard build nodeIdForHostedEnvironment is always null, and desktop Hub-relay nodes already use a per-environment config from their own subscribeConfig stream, so only the hosted-hub web build still pays getConfig. They also missed the duplicate sequential read in agentHandoff.ts.
